state.instructions: Review a maintenance recovery choice with all supplied evidence; classification cannot establish executable correctness.
state.facts: Room ownership remains in CanRent. A repair freezes block_resource, block_source, interval and release evidence. Transport may be unknown after provider acceptance. The provider is being authored to treat identical downtime/restore requests idempotently and emit source-correlated monotone changed outcomes. A maintenance_manager with can_work controls recovery. Reopening must not race an uncertain release; previous completion remains history.
state.actual_code: scenario block(repair:Repair,from:datetime,until:datetime?) by=maintenance_manager; require can_work(actor,repair.parent.location) and repair.parent.resource!=null and repair.state!=fixed and repair.block_state in [none,released] and (until==null or from<until); scenario verify(repair:Repair,evidence:text) by=maintenance_manager; require can_work(actor,repair.parent.location) and repair.state==awaiting_verification and repair.completion!=null and trim(evidence)!=""; RoomsV1.downtime(source:text,resource:text,from:datetime,until:datetime?)->std.OperationOutcome; RoomsV1.restore(source:text,resource:text,evidence:text)->std.OperationOutcome; RoomsV1.changed{value:OperationOutcome}

recovery.instructions: Which recovery strategy best maintains source correlation and recoverability under uncertain acceptance?

criteria.frozen: Reuse the frozen source/resource/payload when an authorized manager retries, correlate the current delivery, and accept verified newer source outcomes. This needs explicit idempotent provider handlers and cannot prove eventual delivery.
criteria.new_source: Allocate a new business source for each recovery request. This isolates attempt identity but can create a second independent block after unknown acceptance and makes release targeting harder.
